Hi Sara / Ben 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone has the same view and to surface next steps:

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary concern: strict access controls around customer data (RBAC, least-privilege) and tight controls for Redwoodsupport access.
- Logging/audit requirements: retention for security and compliance purposes, needs to be tamper-evident and exportable (you mentioned legal may require multi-year retention).
- Data residency: production data must remain in US regions; for backups you noted a preference to keep within US as well.

Open questions we promised to follow up on:
1) Support access model: break-glass process, approval flow, and how access is recorded.
2) RBAC: which roles you need off-the-shelf vs custom roles (e.g., analytics-only, support-readonly, admin).
3) Audit log retention targets (you mentioned 7 years as an upper bound can you confirm if that is required or optional?).
4) SCIM/SSO details: do you require SCIM provisioning and enforced SSO for all users?

Attachments: access_controls_one-pager.pdf (overview), SOC2_summary.pdf (controls we can share).

Proposed next steps:
- Our security deep-dive meeting: 60 minutes with your security + legal and our security/infra team. Proposed slots: Thu 3/11 10am-11am PT or Fri 3/12 1pm-2pm PT  let me know what works.
- Ethan will follow up with a short tech note on support-access mechanics and logging/export options (cc'd).
- If possible, please start the security questionnaire (attached) and add comments where you need more detail.

Thanks looking forward to continuing the conversation.

Thanks Marissa  great summary. Quick answers / clarifications from our side:

- Retention: For audit logs tied to customer financial transactions we have a policy of retaining records up to 7 years. For application-level request logs we can be flexible (3 years preferred, but 7 is acceptable for high-risk telemetry).
- Support access: We require a documented break-glass flow where Redwoodsupport requests access and a named FinTrust approver (can be an on-call engineer or security manager) approves. Access should be time-limited (maximum 8 hours) and all access must be fully audited (who, why, duration, commands/queries run).
- RBAC: We want the ability to create custom roles and ensure principle of least-privilege. Off-the-shelf roles are fine if they can be mirrored to our internal role names via SCIM group mapping.
- Data residency: Confirmed US-only for production; backups should be restricted to US as well unless otherwise agreed.

We'll loop in Legal and Security for the deep-dive. Attaching the security questionnaire  please populate and return.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Liu
Director, Security & Compliance
FinTrust

Hi Sara / team  following up with technical details on the specific items you asked about. Short version up top, details below.

Summary:
- Support access: We offer an audited "break-glass" workflow where support engineers request elevated access. Access is granted only after customer approval (via pre-configured approvers or an on-call rota) and is time-limited by default (configurable TTL, default 4 hours). All sessions are logged and tied to the engineer identity.
- Session capture & audit: We capture request/response metadata and session commands for support investigations. Sensitive payloads can be redacted; we can stream logs to your SIEM (Syslog/HTTPS) or provide export bundles.
- RBAC & provisioning: Role-based controls with custom roles and SCIM group mapping supported. You can map your internal groups to our roles and we honor group-based entitlement.
- Retention: Audit/log retention is configurable per-customer. Standard plan supports 1-3 years; extended retention to 7 years can be provided as an add-on or via log export/archival to your cloud bucket.
- Break-glass approvals: We support both manual approval and integration with PagerDuty/Okta workflows for automated approvals to named approvers. Every break-glass event generates an immutable audit record and an email + webhook notification.

Attached is an architecture sketch for the supported access flow. We'll discuss options to meet your 7-year retention need (export + cold storage vs hosted retention).

Next steps from engineering side:
- If you prefer hosted retention to 7 years we can produce a quote for extended retention. Otherwise we can provide a daily export to your S3/GCS with manifest files for long-term archival.
- For the deep-dive please include your security engineer and legal. I'm happy to cover the flow and instrumentation.

Ethan Park
